title: What's getting more expensive in Malaysia?
subtitle: Inflation by category, where prices are rising fastest, 2026
question: What is Malaysia's inflation rate, and what's getting more expensive?
answer: Malaysia's headline inflation was +2.0% year-on-year as of May 2026, moderate overall, but the squeeze is uneven. Insurance & finance (+4.9%), personal care (+4.8%) and transport (+3.8%) rose fastest, while clothing actually got slightly cheaper.

source.notes: Year-on-year change in the Consumer Price Index by COICOP division, May 2026 vs May 2025. The CPI tracks the average price of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by Malaysian households.

by_category.title: Price change by category, year-on-year
by_category.note: How much each part of the household basket changed in the year to May 2026. Services and transport are rising fastest; clothing slipped.
by_category.ref: CPI by COICOP division, May 2026 vs May 2025

takeaways: Overall prices rose **+2.0%** in the year to May 2026, moderate, and below Malaysia's long-run average.
The real squeeze is in **services**: insurance & finance (+4.9%), personal care (+4.8%) and **transport (+3.8%)** led the gains.
Everyday **food** rose a milder **+1.4%**, and **clothing** was the only category to get *cheaper* (−0.1%).
"Headline inflation" is an average, your personal rate depends on what you spend on. A heavy driver feels transport; a renter feels housing.

faq.a: Malaysia's headline inflation (CPI) was +2.0% year-on-year as of May 2026, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).

faq.q: What is getting more expensive in Malaysia?
faq.a: In the year to May 2026, insurance & finance (+4.9%), personal care (+4.8%) and transport (+3.8%) rose fastest. Food rose a milder +1.4%, and clothing got slightly cheaper.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change over time in the prices Malaysian households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. DOSM publishes it monthly.
